**Battle of Waterloo (18 June 1815)**  
*Approximate total casualties:* **≈ 25 000–30 000**

| Side | Approximate killed & wounded |
|------|------------------------------|
| French army (under Napoleon) | ~12 500‑13 000 |
| Anglo‑Dutch/Prussian coalition forces (British, Dutch, Belgian, German, Prussians under Wellington & Blücher) | ~15 000‑17 000 |

> *Sources*: Historical estimates vary slightly depending on which casualty lists are consulted. Commonly cited figures come from contemporary military reports and later scholarly compilations such as:
> - J.E.A. Sutherland’s “A History of the War” (1910)
> - A.J.P. Taylor’s “The Waterloo Campaign” (1969)
> - Modern analyses like David G. Chandler’s “Waterloo: The Final Duel” (1972)

These totals include those who were killed outright or mortally wounded, plus those wounded but survived; they exclude missing soldiers whose status was uncertain at the time. Casualty counts can differ by several hundred due to incomplete records and differing definitions of "wounded."
